summary.one_liner: choose is a human-friendly command-line tool, written in Rust, that selects fields from each line of text as an alternative to cut and sometimes awk.
summary.what_it_does: It prints chosen fields from lines of input using a short, Python-list-slice-like syntax (for example 5, 2:5, :3, 3:, -1, -3:-1). Indexing is zero-based and negative indices count from the end of the line. Ranges can be inclusive or exclusive (via -x), and reverse ranges are supported. The default field separator is whitespace, and -f accepts a regular expression separator using Rust's regex syntax. Other options include character-wise selection (-c), non-greedy separators (-n), a custom output separator (-o), reading from a file (-i), and a debug mode (-d). The README says it is slightly faster than cut on sufficiently long inputs and much faster than awk.
use_cases: select columns from whitespace-delimited command output
extract the nth field from colon-separated lines
print the last few fields of each line
pull fields out of log lines with a regex separator
replace simple cut or awk one-liners in shell scripts
select characters by position instead of fields
how_to_run: git clone <repository-url> && cd choose && cargo build --release
notable: Python-style list slice syntax for field selection, including negative indices from end of line
Regular expression field separators via -f, using Rust regex syntax
Benchmarked as faster than cut for long inputs and much faster than awk, per the README
caveats: Not meant as a drop-in or complete replacement for cut or awk, per the README
Building from source requires the Rust toolchain
